{{Short description|Head of the Australian Bureau of Statistics}}
The '''Australian Statistician''' is the head of the [[Australian Bureau of Statistics]].

On 18 June 1906, the first ''Statistician of the Commonwealth of Australia'' was appointed to carry out the provisions of the ''Census and Statistics Act 1905''. Later in the same year the Commonwealth Bureau of Census and Statistics was formed (renamed the Australian Bureau of Statistics in 1975).<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://assda.anu.edu.au/census/c86/hatac86/section1.html |title=CENSUS 86 - How Australia Takes a Census |access-date=2006-06-04 |archive-date=2006-05-21 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060521021340/http://assda.anu.edu.au/census/c86/hatac86/section1.html |url-status=dead }}</ref>

[[Timothy Augustine Coghlan]] was offered the position in December 1905, but had to decline due to his obligations to the New South Wales government.<ref>{{cite thesis|url=https://openresearch-repository.anu.edu.au/bitstream/1885/112133/4/b12930623_Carment_David_Sulman.pdf|title=Australian liberal: a political biography of Sir Littleton Groom, 1867-1936|first=David|last=Carment|year=1975|publisher=[[Australian National University]]|type=PhD thesis|pages=47–49}}</ref>

==Commonwealth Statisticians==
* [[George Handley Knibbs]] (1906&ndash;1921<ref>{{Cite Australian Dictionary of Biography |first=Susan |last=Bambrick |title=Sir George Handley Knibbs (1858–1929) |id2=knibbs-sir-george-handley-6985 |year=1983 |volume=9 |access-date=25 August 2025}}</ref>)
* [[Charles Henry Wickens]] (August 1922 &ndash; April 1932,<ref>{{Cite Australian Dictionary of Biography |first1=Cameron |last1=Hazlehurst |first2=Margot |last2=Kerley |title=Charles Henry Wickens (1872–1939) |id2=wickens-charles-henry-9091 |year=1990 |volume=12 |access-date=25 August 2025}}</ref> although [[Lyndhurst Falkiner Giblin]] was appointed acting Commonwealth Statistician following Wickens' stroke in 1931<ref name="building ABS">[http://www.abs.gov.au/Ausstats/abs@.nsf/90a12181d877a6a6ca2568b5007b861c/c5e5a2d6d96d1aafca256f720083303c!OpenDocument Building a national statistical agency: From the Commonwealth Bureau of Census and Statistics to the Australian Bureau of Statistics]</ref>)
* [[Edward Tannock McPhee]] (1933&ndash;1936)<ref name="building ABS"/>
* [[Roland Wilson (economist)|Sir Roland Wilson]] (1936&ndash;1940; 1946&ndash;1951)<ref name="building ABS"/>
* Sir [[Stanley Roy Carver]] (acting from 1940<ref name="Carver bio"/> to 1946, and again from 1948 to 1951. Formally appointed Commonwealth Statistician from 20 August 1957 to 1961<ref name="building ABS"/> or 6 February 1962<ref name="Carver bio">{{Cite Australian Dictionary of Biography |first=Margot |last=Kerley |title=Sir Stanley Roy Carver (1897–1967) |id2=carver-sir-stanley-roy-9704 |year=1993 |volume=13 |access-date=25 August 2025}}</ref>)
* [[Keith Archer]] (1962&ndash;1970)<ref name="building ABS"/>
* [[Jack O'Neill (statistician)|Jack O'Neill]] (acting from 1969–1972. Commonwealth Statistician from 1972&ndash;1975)
